statements.subject: connection
statements.description: 220 Service ready for new user. This is identical to the state in which a user finds himself immediately after the control connection is opened.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: 331 User name okay, need password. Intermediate state in the login command sequence after the USER command is accepted.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: 332 Need account for login. Intermediate state when account information is required for login, entered after a successful PASS command.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: 230 User logged in, proceed. The user is authenticated; a new FTP service request may be initiated.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: 1yz Positive Preliminary reply: The requested action is being initiated; expect another reply before proceeding with a new command. Represents the state of an FTP service command in progress.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: 350 Requested file action pending further information. Intermediate state used in command sequence groups such as RNFR/RNTO and REST/service-command.
statements.state_name: Requested file action pending further information

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: 221 Service closing control connection. Logged out if appropriate. 421 Service not available, closing control connection.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: The communication channel from the user-PI to the server-PI is established as a TCP connection from the user to the standard server port. Server sends 220 Service ready for new user.
statements.trigger: TCP connection established to standard server port

statements.subject: session
statements.description: USER NAME (USER): This command will normally be the first command transmitted by the user after the control connections are made. Server responds 331 User name okay, need password.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: Servers may allow a new USER command to be entered at any point in order to change the access control and/or accounting information. This has the effect of flushing any user, password, and account information already supplied and beginning the login sequence again. All transfer parameters are unchanged and any file transfer in progress is completed under the old access control parameters.
actions: complete any transfer in progress under old access control parameters

statements.subject: session
statements.description: If account information is NOT required for login, the reply to a successful PASSword command is 230 User logged in, proceed.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: When account information is required for login, the response to a successful PASSword command is reply code 332 Need account for login.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: ACCOUNT (ACCT) command completes login when account is required: successful account information provided after 332 reply leads to logged-in state (230 User logged in, proceed).

statements.subject: session
statements.description: A failure at any point in the sequence necessitates the repetition of the entire sequence from the beginning. The replies show the existence of an intermediate state if all preceding commands have been successful.
statements.trigger: 4yz or 5yz reply to command in login sequence
actions: repeat entire login sequence from beginning

statements.subject: session
statements.description: REINITIALIZE (REIN): This command terminates a USER, flushing all I/O and account information, except to allow any transfer in progress to be completed. All parameters are reset to the default settings and the control connection is left open. This is identical to the state in which a user finds himself immediately after the control connection is opened.
actions: allow any transfer in progress to complete

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: LOGOUT (QUIT): This command terminates a USER and if file transfer is not in progress, the server closes the control connection.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: LOGOUT (QUIT): If file transfer is in progress, the connection will remain open for result response and the server will then close it.
actions: keep control connection open for result response
close control connection after transfer result

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: An unexpected close on the control connection will cause the server to take the effective action of an abort (ABOR) and a logout (QUIT).

statements.subject: session
statements.description: FTP service command causes server-DTP to initiate data transfer; server sends 1yz Positive Preliminary reply. The requested action is being initiated; expect another reply before proceeding with a new command.
statements.trigger: FTP service command (RETR, STOR, STOU, APPE, LIST, NLST)

statements.subject: session
statements.description: 2yz Positive Completion reply: The requested action has been successfully completed. A new request may be initiated. 226 Closing data connection. Requested file action successful.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: ABORT (ABOR) case 1: The FTP service command was already completed. The server closes the data connection (if it is open) and responds with a 226 reply, indicating that the abort command was successfully processed.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: ABORT (ABOR) case 2: The FTP service command is still in progress. The server aborts the FTP service in progress and closes the data connection, returning a 426 reply to indicate that the service request terminated abnormally. The server then sends a 226 reply, indicating that the abort command was successfully processed.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: RENAME FROM (RNFR): This command must be immediately followed by a rename to command specifying the new file pathname. Reply 350 Requested file action pending further information.
statements.to_state: Requested file action pending further information

statements.subject: session
statements.description: RENAME TO (RNTO): This command specifies the new pathname of the file specified in the immediately preceding rename from command. Together the two commands cause a file to be renamed. Reply 250 Requested file action okay, completed.
statements.from_state: Requested file action pending further information

statements.subject: session
statements.description: RESTART (REST): This command does not cause file transfer but skips over the file to the specified data checkpoint. This command shall be immediately followed by the appropriate FTP service command which shall cause file transfer to resume. Reply 350.
statements.to_state: Requested file action pending further information

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: 421 Service not available, closing control connection. This may be a reply to any command if the service knows it must shut down.

statements.subject: message
statements.description: PASSWORD (PASS): This command must be immediately preceded by the user name command.

statements.subject: message
statements.description: The commands may be in any order except that a rename from command must be followed by a rename to command.
statements.guard_semantics: session.state = <Requested file action pending further information>

statements.subject: message
statements.description: The restart command must be followed by the interrupted service command (e.g., STOR or RETR). This command shall be immediately followed by the appropriate FTP service command which shall cause file transfer to resume.
statements.guard_semantics: session.state = <Requested file action pending further information>

statements.subject: message
statements.description: Transfer parameter commands may be in any order except that they must precede the FTP service request.
statements.object_name: transfer parameter commands (PORT, PASV, TYPE, STRU, MODE)

statements.subject: message
statements.description: ALLOCATE (ALLO): This command shall be followed by a STORe or APPEnd command.
statements.guard_semantics: ALLO must be followed by STOR | APPE
